Finding PRRT_kwDOUKOPKc6h9j8q is the strongest: the completeness refusal landed only in checkMerge and not in pr-ready.mjs's --show path, but its exposure is a self-closing one-hour window for receipts minted before this change, its outcome is a visibly-short receipt block rather than silent data loss, and it cannot affect this PR's own carve-out merge, whose receipt will be minted from this branch's code. Findings PRRT_kwDOUKOPKc6h9j8u and PRRT_kwDOUKOPKc6h9j8z each require a compound low-probability precondition (a load-time crash of fable-dispatch, or a close-out poll landing between the receipt write and a publish that then fails), so buying a round -- which on a budget of 3 would consume the entire remaining allowance plus its mandatory review round -- is not worth it against an artifact class whose failure mode is wrongly-blocking.

A READY receipt minted before the translations item existed really would have been honoured by the merge hook inside its one-hour window, and the diff fixes exactly that at core/scripts/guard-decision.mjs @@ -1718,6 +1718,22 @@.

The premise holds against the patch -- the item-presence refusal was added only to checkMerge in guard-decision.mjs, and pr-ready.mjs's --show path is untouched by the diff -- so the same defect the previous round fixed survives in its sibling consumer, which is the general-mechanism half of the round-1 finding.

roundState checks receipts first and returns "done" with no further evidence, so if the receipt is written before the page publish as the finding states, a permanently-failed publish leaves a round reading 'accounted' forever; this is a defect in the increment's own completion signal rather than a demand for unobservable delivery proof.
